checked_sources.label: Batch 133 raw source capture - Solar Shading Fundamentals
checked_sources.description: Local raw-source-layer capture for Solar Shading Fundamentals; includes checked TOA 4 locators and official-source URL locators. Claims cite this artifact hash.
checked_markdown_lines: TOA 4 lines 692-810 explain orientation, sun-path diagrams, azimuth, altitude, date lines, airflow, and Philippine prevailing wind seasons.
TOA 4 lines 1199-1247 and 1302-1352 list overhangs, louvers, eggcrate/brise-soleil, skylights, light shelves, and clerestories.
NOAA Solar Calculator glossary, https://gml.noaa.gov/grad/solcalc/glossary.html, lines 90-91 and 150-154: azimuth/elevation locate sky position and solar declination varies seasonally.

WBDG Sun Control and Shading Devices, https://www.wbdg.org/resources/sun-control-and-shading-devices, lines 80-87, 105-108, 125-143, and 150-160: shading controls heat gain, glare, daylight, sun angles, latitude transfer, and maintenance risk.
WBDG Daylighting, https://www.wbdg.org/resources/daylighting, lines 113-128 and 191-202: light shelves and louvers redirect daylight, reduce glare, and vary by orientation.
checked_sources.local_audit_note: Official web sources are used only through the locally captured source map; article and question claims cite local artifacts.

classification.scenario_policy_reason: For a west-facing library reading room, the architect avoids relying on a simple horizontal overhang alone. The study tests vertical fins, adjustable louvers, glare control, daylight penetration, maintenance access, and a clear ventilation path before selecting the final shading system.
